topic: They only listen when I yell: give the direction once, the CDC way

photo.author: Ivan S
photo.alt: Mom and son enjoying playtime indoors with wooden toys, capturing the essence of family bonding.

caption:
"Not doing a single thing I ask." If your child ignores you until you yell, you are not alone, and it is not because you are too soft or too harsh.

The CDC describes 4 simple steps for giving directions to your child: get on their level and say their name, say what TO do, check, then follow through calmly.

Save this and send it to a co-parent so you both say it the same way.

Comment LISTEN and I’ll send the link straight to you.

slides.text:
My child ignores me until I yell. Not doing a single thing I ask.

**Here is how to say it once and be heard.**

You've asked nicely. Counted to three. Asked again and again.

And you still end up yelling.

**That does not make you a bad parent.** Often it is the way the direction is given that needs a small change, not your child or your heart.

**Step 1: Get their attention first.**

Squat or sit next to your child, face to face. Use their name and eye contact.

Say: **"Maya, look at me for a second."**

**Step 2: Say what TO do.**

The CDC suggests clear, positive directions instead of "stop" or "don't", starting with "please".

Instead of "Stop running!" say: **"Please walk next to me."**

**Step 3: Check if it happened.**

Give them a moment, then look. Watch for stalling or partly doing it.

Keep your voice neutral. **One direction at a time** works best for short attention spans.

Say: **"I see your shoes are still off. Shoes on, please."**

**Step 4: Follow through, calmly.**

When they do it, notice it: **"You put your shoes on. Thank you!"**

When they don't, calmly do what you said would happen, the same way each time. Consistency is what builds trust.

**Will yelling get it done?**

The AAP notes that harsh verbal discipline may lead to more behavior problems over time. You are not a bad parent for yelling, and you can change it.

If you feel overwhelmed, pause, take a few deep breaths, then try the 4 steps again.

**Try this today:**

Pick just ONE daily moment, like shoes or bath time. Use all 4 steps, once, with a calm voice.

Reminder: expectations should fit their age. **Small steps count.**
